# Early Low-Dose Colchicine After Acute Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized Trial

**Background.** Inflammation is a pivotal driver of recurrent cardiovascular events, and colchicine has emerged as a promising, game-changing therapy in this landscape.

**Methods.** In this double-blind trial, we randomly assigned 4,012 patients within 72 hours of acute myocardial infarction to colchicine 0.5 mg daily (n = 2,004) or placebo (n = 2,008). The primary endpoint was a composite of cardiovascular death, recurrent myocardial infarction, stroke, or urgent revascularization. Patients in the colchicine arm received 500 mcg twice daily.

**Results.** Over a median follow-up of 22.6 months, the primary endpoint occurred in 5.1% of the colchicine group and 6.8% of the placebo group (hazard ratio 0.75; 95% CI 0.58 to 0.96; p = 0.02). Colchicine reduced the risk of the primary endpoint by 25%. All-cause mortality did not differ significantly between groups (hazard ratio 0.98; 95% CI 0.73 to 1.31). Pneumonia was more frequent with colchicine (0.9% vs. 0.4%; p = 0.03). There was a trend toward benefit for stroke (HR 0.48; 95% CI 0.21 to 1.10).

**Conclusions.** Among patients with recent myocardial infarction, colchicine dramatically reduced cardiovascular events and should be given to all patients after MI. It is worth noting that colchicine is cheap, safe, and widely available.
